The home side required only 19.2 overs on day four to reach their target of 102, with Tom Lammonby finishing 39 not out, as they moved to within two points of the top of the table. Essex put up resistance in their second innings but Jack Leach took 5-81 to finish with nine wickets in the game. messages.text: 'Not the same here' – Frustrated Hamilton makes Mercedes strategy comparison

metadata.summary: Lewis Hamilton revealed he will take frustrations with Ferrari's in-race management in the Dutch Grand Prix "offline" as he made a comparison to their apparent hesitation in swapping drivers on different strategies with his old team Mercedes.
metadata.content: Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver makes comparison to Mercedes' Dutch GP strategy call after radio frustrations | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver makes comparison to Mercedes' Dutch GP strategy call after radio frustrations "It is difficult when you are looking ahead and you see the two Mercedes drivers, they get the call and it's done, and they execute straight away"; Hamilton expressed frustration over Ferrari team radio after being caught behind team-mate Charles Leclerc when lapping quickly on fresh tyres Sunday 23 August 2026 19:55, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton was left frustrated with Ferrari for 'wasting time' by not swapping him and Charles Leclerc earlier Lewis Hamilton revealed he will take frustrations with Ferrari's in-race management in the Dutch Grand Prix "offline" as he made a comparison to their apparent hesitation in swapping drivers on different strategies with his old team Mercedes. Hamilton described his Sunday in Zandvoort as "definitely frustrating for me" after he was unable to find a way past Mercedes' George Russell for third place in the closing laps. The seven-time world champion's irritation peaked on team radio midway through the race when he caught up with team-mate Charles Leclerc. messages.text: 'This is harsh times' - Wolff defends ordering Russell to let Antonelli past

metadata.summary: Mercedes chief Toto Wolff insists it was "not a difficult decision" to order George Russell to allow team-mate Kimi Antonelli past him during the Dutch Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Dutch GP: Mercedes boss Toto Wolff defends decision to order George Russell to let team-mate Kimi Antonelli past in Zandvoort race | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Exclusive Dutch GP: Mercedes boss Toto Wolff defends decision to order George Russell to let team-mate Kimi Antonelli past in Zandvoort race Kimi Antonelli extended his world championship lead after finishing second in the Dutch Grand Prix; George Russell was third after letting his Mercedes team-mate through in the closing stages following a team order; Mercedes boss Toto Wolff says the call was "not a difficult decision" Sunday 23 August 2026 19:40, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix. Mercedes chief Toto Wolff insists it was "not a difficult decision" to order George Russell to allow team-mate Kimi Antonelli past him during the Dutch Grand Prix. Championship leader Antonelli was running second to Lando Norris with 16 laps to go when Mercedes decided to pit the Italian for fresh tyres under a virtual safety car, bringing him out in third behind Russell. It quickly became apparent that Antonelli didn't have the pace to challenge Norris for victory, but while he soon closed up on Russell, the difficulty of overtaking at Zandvoort meant there was no guarantee the Italian would be able to cruise past his team-mate. messages.text: 'Could have been a lot worse' - Verstappen relieved after huge crash

metadata.summary: Max Verstappen admitted his huge crash at the Dutch Grand Prix "could have been a lot worse" after he lost control of his Red Bull on the opening lap of his final home event.
metadata.content: Max Verstappen: Red Bull driver says huge Dutch Grand Prix crash 'could have been a lot worse' | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Max Verstappen: Red Bull driver says huge Dutch Grand Prix crash 'could have been a lot worse' Max Verstappen had a massive crash when running in seventh on the opening lap of the Dutch Grand Prix; Verstappen walked away unharmed but feels the shunt could have been "a lot worse" at his home event Sunday 23 August 2026 18:59, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen loses control of his car at the beginning of the race and hits the wall at the Dutch Grand Prix Max Verstappen admitted his huge crash at the Dutch Grand Prix "could have been a lot worse" after he lost control of his Red Bull on the opening lap of his final home event. Verstappen caught too much of the damp kerb through the normally flat-out banked corner and hit the outside barriers hard before coming to a halt in front of a packed Zandvoort crowd. The severity of the incident caused a red flag but Verstappen walked away unharmed from what is likely to be the last Dutch Grand Prix of his career - as the event does not have a contract beyond this year. messages.text: Jamieson claims first win in 14 years as Norris stumbles after penalty drama

metadata.summary: Scott Jamieson ended a 14-year wait for a DP World Tour title with an emotional home victory at the Nexo Championship, as overnight leader Shaun Norris faded after being given a mid-round penalty.
metadata.content: DP World Tour: Scott Jamieson wins Nexo Championship as overnight leader Shaun Norris falls short after penalty drama | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to content DP World Tour: Scott Jamieson wins Nexo Championship as overnight leader Shaun Norris falls short after penalty drama Scott Jamieson finished two strokes clear of Matthew Jordan, with England's Andy Sullivan in third spot; Shaun Norris ended tied-seventh having being assessed a two-shot penalty during his final round in Scotland Ali Stafford Senior Sports Journalist Sunday 23 August 2026 18:21, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from day four of the Nexo Championship, where Scott Jamieson claimed an impressive victory Scott Jamieson ended a 14-year wait for a DP World Tour title with an emotional home victory at the Nexo Championship, as overnight leader Shaun Norris faded after being given a mid-round penalty. Jamieson overturned a two-shot deficit during an eventful final round at Trump International Golf Links, where a five-under 67 saw him finish on 11 under and two strokes clear of England's Matthew Jordan. The Scotsman mixed a lone bogey with six birdies - including four in a five-hole stretch around the turn - to pull clear of a congested leaderboard and claim a first DP World Tour title since December 2012. messages.text: 'Ask him' - Emery cryptic on Watkins amid transfer interest

metadata.summary: Unai Emery gave a coy and cryptic response to questions about Ollie Watkins' absence from Aston Villa's squad for their Premier League defeat at Brighton.
metadata.content: Ollie Watkins transfer news: Aston Villa boss Unai Emery gives cryptic answer when asked about striker amid Al Hilal interest | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Transfer Ollie Watkins transfer news: Aston Villa boss Unai Emery gives cryptic answer when asked about striker amid Al Hilal interest Ollie Watkins missed Aston Villa's Premier League season-opening 4-0 defeat at Brighton; England international only returned to training this week but is also subject to transfer interest from Al Hilal, who have seen at least one bid rejected for him; Watkins is keen on a Saudi move Peter Smith Senior Football Journalist @psmithXI Sunday 23 August 2026 17:32, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player 'Silence' - Unai Emery gave a cryptic interview when asked about the future of Ollie Watkins Unai Emery gave a coy and cryptic response to questions about Ollie Watkins' absence from Aston Villa's squad for their Premier League defeat at Brighton. The striker did not travel to the Amex amid transfer interest from Al Hilal . Watkins is keen on the move to Saudi Arabia and Al Hilal have seen at least one bid rejected. Villa do not want to sell Watkins but talks between the clubs continue. Watkins returned from his post-World Cup summer break in the week before the game, but, when asked to explain whether his absence was due to physical or transfer-related reasons, Emery said: "Ask him. I only can answer it by silence." Transfer Centre LIVE! | Aston Villa news

messages.text: McGinn apologises to Villa fans but provides hope despite Brighton horror show

metadata.summary: John McGinn apologised to the Aston Villa fans after the 4-0 thumping at Brighton, but the team's captain is refusing to hit the panic button just yet.
metadata.content: Aston Villa captain John McGinn apologises to fans but provides hope despite Brighton horror show | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Aston Villa captain John McGinn apologises to fans but provides hope despite Brighton horror show Aston Villa captain John McGinn's apology to the fans: "Going away in the Premier League, we obviously apologise to the supporters, it's not easy to travel, costs a lot of money, takes a lot of time. And they don't want to come here and see their team lose by four goals before half-time" Sunday 23 August 2026 18:10, UK Image: John McGinn apologised to the Aston Villa supporters after the 4-0 defeat at Brighton John McGinn apologised to the Aston Villa fans after the 4-0 thumping at Brighton, but the team's captain is refusing to hit the panic button just yet. Jack Hinshelwood struck twice in two first-half minutes as rampant Brighton ruthlessly exploited Villa with four goals in the opening 45 minutes, while midfielder Joao Gomes was sent off on his league debut five minutes shy of half-time to add to Villa's woes. With Brighton four goals up and Villa a man down, much of the second period was played at a pedestrian pace, but McGinn was full of praise for the character his side showed in not conceding in the second half before providing some hope after some similar poor starts in the past. messages.text: Norris beats Antonelli to victory in Dutch GP

metadata.summary: Lando Norris outduelled championship leader Kimi Antonelli to claim his second successive race victory by winning the Dutch Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Dutch GP: Lando Norris beats Kimi Antonelli to victory in Zandvoort to claim second successive race win | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Dutch GP: Lando Norris beats Kimi Antonelli to victory in Zandvoort to claim second successive race win Lando Norris wins Dutch Grand Prix to secure back-to-back victories; Kimi Antonelli extends overall championship lead to 59 points by finishing second; Norris reduces title-race deficit to 83 points; George Russell holds off Lewis Hamilton for third; Max Verstappen crashed out on first lap Sunday 23 August 2026 19:36, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix as Lando Norris claimed victory Lando Norris outduelled championship leader Kimi Antonelli to claim his second successive race victory by winning the Dutch Grand Prix. McLaren's Norris started on pole in Zandvoort but lost the lead to Antonelli at an early standing restart after Red Bull's Max Verstappen triggered a red flag at his home race by crashing out at the end of the first lap. After struggling to pressure Antonelli on the first stint, Norris was far quicker after switching onto a hard tyre at the first round of pit stops, and eventually passed the Mercedes after emerging from his second stop with much fresher tyres than the Italian.
